anlamlar.en: to do something because of advice, information or a feeling
ornekler: The police acted on a tip from a neighbor.
You should act on your doctor's advice.

anlamlar.en: to behave badly, or to not work properly
ornekler: The kids always act up when they're tired.
My laptop is acting up again.

anlamlar.en: to reply rudely to someone in authority
ornekler: Don't answer back when your teacher is talking to you.
He was punished for answering back.

anlamlar.en: to ask several people for information or help
ornekler: I'll ask around and see if anyone has a spare bike.
She asked around for a good dentist.

anlamlar.en: to suddenly become unconscious
ornekler: He blacked out and fell to the floor.
I must have blacked out for a few seconds.

anlamlar.en: to become less strong and then end
ornekler: The storm blew over during the night.
Don't worry, the argument will soon blow over.

anlamlar.en: to not allow yourself to show strong feelings
ornekler: It's not healthy to bottle up your anger.
She bottled up her feelings for years.

anlamlar.tr: -e yol açmak, tetiklemek (genellikle kötü bir şey)
anlamlar.en: to cause something to happen, usually something bad
ornekler: Stress can bring on headaches.
What brought on this sudden change?

anlamlar.en: to use a success or achievement as a base for further progress
ornekler: We need to build on last year's success.
The course builds on what you learned before.

anlamlar.en: to suddenly start to do something, especially crying or laughing
ornekler: She burst into tears.
The audience burst into laughter.

anlamlar.en: to enter a place suddenly and with force
ornekler: He burst into the room without knocking.
The police burst into the house.

anlamlar.en: to suddenly start to laugh, cry or say something
ornekler: Everyone burst out laughing.
"That's not fair!" she burst out.

anlamlar.en: to shout or say something loudly
ornekler: The teacher called out the names.
Someone called out my name from across the street.

anlamlar.en: to publicly criticize someone for something wrong they have done
ornekler: She called out the company for its unfair pay.
It's important to call out bad behavior.

anlamlar.en: to continue to exist or have an effect in a different situation or period
ornekler: You can carry over five days of vacation to next year.
Habits from school often carry over into adult life.

anlamlar.en: to discover that someone has made a mistake, or to put someone in a difficult situation
ornekler: The tricky question caught many students out.
We were caught out by the sudden rain.

anlamlar.en: to gradually surround or come nearer to someone or something
ornekler: The police were closing in on the thief.
Darkness closed in around us.

anlamlar.en: to manage to get something that is difficult to get
ornekler: Good jobs are hard to come by.
How did you come by this old map?

anlamlar.en: to visit a place for a short time
ornekler: Come by my office this afternoon.
She came by to say hello.

anlamlar.tr: -e dayanmak, -den ibaret olmak, sonunda -e bağlı olmak
anlamlar.en: to be the most important thing that decides a situation
ornekler: In the end, it comes down to money.
It all comes down to how hard you work.

anlamlar.en: to receive criticism or blame
ornekler: The government has come in for a lot of criticism.
The film came in for some harsh reviews.

anlamlar.en: to receive money or property after someone has died
ornekler: She came into a lot of money when her aunt died.
He came into a fortune at 21.

anlamlar.en: to be involved or have an effect
ornekler: Where does money come into it?
Luck didn't come into it – she worked hard.

anlamlar.en: to say something suddenly, especially something surprising
ornekler: Kids come out with the funniest things.
He came out with a really strange idea.

anlamlar.en: to reach a particular total
ornekler: The bill came to $45.
The total comes to about 200 people.

anlamlar.en: to become conscious again
ornekler: When I came to, I was in hospital.
He came to after a few minutes.

anlamlar.en: to reach a decision or conclusion
ornekler: We came to the conclusion that he was lying.
They finally came to an agreement.

anlamlar.en: to become cooler
ornekler: We went for a swim to cool off.
Let the engine cool off before you touch it.

anlamlar.en: to become calmer after being angry
ornekler: Give him time to cool off.
Let's take a break and cool off.

anlamlar.en: to count backwards to zero before an event
ornekler: The crowd counted down the last ten seconds of the year.
We're counting down the days until the holidays.

anlamlar.en: to include someone in an activity
ornekler: If you're going to the beach, count me in!
Can we count you in for dinner?

anlamlar.en: to not include someone in an activity
ornekler: If it's another long meeting, count me out.
Don't count him out yet – he can still win.

anlamlar.en: to quickly deal with something that is causing problems
ornekler: We need to cut through the paperwork.
Her clear answer cut through the confusion.

anlamlar.en: to go through a place, especially as a shorter way
ornekler: We cut through the park to get home.
The road cuts through the forest.

anlamlar.tr: (bir gerçek) aklına dank etmek, fark etmek
anlamlar.en: to become clear to someone for the first time
ornekler: It suddenly dawned on me that I had left my keys at home.
It never dawned on her that he was lying.

anlamlar.en: to gradually become quieter and then stop
ornekler: The sound of the car died away.
The wind died away at night.

anlamlar.en: to die one by one until there are none left
ornekler: The old trees are slowly dying off.
Many fish died off in the hot summer.

anlamlar.en: to do something again
ornekler: Your homework is too messy – do it over.
If I could do it over, I would choose differently.

anlamlar.en: to make something last longer than necessary
ornekler: Let's not drag out this discussion.
They dragged out the negotiations for months.

anlamlar.en: to invent something unusual or new
ornekler: Who dreamed up this crazy idea?
She dreamed up a story for the children.

anlamlar.en: to gradually fall asleep
ornekler: I drifted off while watching TV.
The baby drifted off in my arms.

anlamlar.en: to make a sound impossible to hear by making a louder noise
ornekler: The music drowned out our conversation.
His voice was drowned out by the crowd.

anlamlar.tr: (üzücü bir şey üzerinde) durmak, kafaya takmak
anlamlar.en: to keep thinking or talking about something, especially something bad
ornekler: Don't dwell on your mistakes.
There's no point dwelling on the past.

anlamlar.en: to become less strong or unpleasant, or to do something less
ornekler: The rain eased off in the afternoon.
You should ease off a bit – you're working too hard.

anlamlar.en: to use or take away a large part of something valuable
ornekler: The repairs ate into our savings.
Long meetings eat into my working time.

anlamlar.en: to eat all of something
ornekler: Eat up your vegetables!
The kids ate up all the cake.

anlamlar.en: to use a lot of something
ornekler: This old car eats up gas.
Traveling to work eats up two hours a day.

anlamlar.en: to have a particular result or ending
ornekler: The match ended in a draw.
Their marriage ended in divorce.

anlamlar.en: to become level or equal, or to make something level or equal
ornekler: Prices should even out over the year.
We tried to even out the workload.

anlamlar.en: to use something or someone for help when other things have failed
ornekler: We have some savings to fall back on.
When all else failed, he fell back on his old skills.

anlamlar.en: to be part of a particular group
ornekler: These animals fall into two groups.
Most students fall into this category.

anlamlar.en: to start to be in a particular state or habit
ornekler: He fell into a deep sleep.
She fell into the habit of eating late.

anlamlar.en: to defend yourself against someone or something
ornekler: She fended off the attack with her umbrella.
The minister fended off difficult questions.

anlamlar.en: to stop someone or something from attacking you, or to get rid of an illness
ornekler: She managed to fight off her attacker.
Vitamin C helps the body fight off colds.

anlamlar.en: to be part of a group or situation, or to be the right size for a space
ornekler: How does this piece fit into the puzzle?
He never really fitted into the team.

anlamlar.en: to gradually end in a weak or disappointing way
ornekler: The protest fizzled out after a few days.
Their romance quickly fizzled out.

anlamlar.en: to suddenly start again or become worse
ornekler: Fighting flared up again in the north.
His back problem flares up in winter.

anlamlar.tr: (bir işi) sonuna kadar götürmek, arkasını getirmek
anlamlar.en: to complete something that you have started or promised
ornekler: It's a good plan, but will they follow it through?
You need to follow through on your promises.

anlamlar.en: to spend a lot of money on something, especially unwillingly
ornekler: We had to fork out $500 for the repairs.
I'm not forking out for a new phone.

anlamlar.en: to disapprove of something
ornekler: Using phones in class is frowned on.
My parents frown on staying out late.

anlamlar.en: to do something unpleasant to someone because they have done something unpleasant to you
ornekler: He wanted to get back at his brother for the joke.
She's trying to get back at me.

anlamlar.en: to fail to do as much work or pay as much money as you should by a particular time
ornekler: I got behind with my studies when I was ill.
Don't get behind with the rent.

anlamlar.en: to support a person or idea
ornekler: The whole town got behind the team.
We need to get behind this project.

anlamlar.en: to do something that you have intended to do for a long time
ornekler: I finally got round to fixing the door.
I never got round to calling her.

anlamlar.en: to stop hoping that someone or something will succeed or change
ornekler: Don't give up on me – I'll do better.
The doctors never gave up on him.

anlamlar.en: to break or fall down because of pressure
ornekler: The bridge gave way under the weight.
Suddenly the floor gave way.

anlamlar.en: to allow other vehicles to go first
ornekler: You must give way to traffic on the right.
Give way to the bus.

anlamlar.en: to be replaced by something, or to stop opposing something
ornekler: Sadness gave way to anger.
The government finally gave way to public pressure.

anlamlar.en: to start to deal with something
ornekler: How do I go about getting a visa?
I'm not sure how to go about this.

anlamlar.en: to continue doing your usual activities
ornekler: People went about their daily lives.
She went about her work quietly.

anlamlar.en: to be opposite to a principle, belief or wish
ornekler: It goes against my beliefs.
He went against his parents' wishes.

anlamlar.en: to be unfavorable to someone
ornekler: The decision went against us.
If the vote goes against him, he'll resign.

anlamlar.en: to spread from one person to another
ornekler: There's a virus going around.
A rumor is going around about her.

anlamlar.en: to be enough for everyone
ornekler: There aren't enough books to go around.
Is there enough food to go around?

anlamlar.en: to describe or explain something in detail
ornekler: I don't want to go into details now.
The book goes into the history of the city.

anlamlar.en: to start working in a particular type of job
ornekler: She wants to go into medicine.
He went into business with his father.

anlamlar.en: to be used or spent for something
ornekler: A lot of work went into this project.
How much money went into the building?

anlamlar.en: to fail financially
ornekler: Many small businesses went under during the crisis.
The company went under last year.

anlamlar.en: to sink below the surface of water
ornekler: The ship went under in minutes.
He went under and didn't come up.

anlamlar.en: to gradually become less close to someone
ornekler: We grew apart after we left school.
The couple slowly grew apart.

anlamlar.en: to develop into a particular type of person or thing
ornekler: She has grown into a confident young woman.
The small shop grew into a big business.

anlamlar.en: to become big enough to fit clothes
ornekler: The coat is too big, but he'll grow into it.
Buy a size bigger – she'll grow into it.

anlamlar.en: to become more liked by someone over time
ornekler: I didn't like the song at first, but it's growing on me.
The town grew on her.

anlamlar.en: to return something to the person who gave it to you
ornekler: The teacher handed back our tests.
Please hand back the keys when you leave.

anlamlar.en: to not move forward, often because you are shy or nervous
ornekler: She hung back while the others went in.
Don't hang back – come and join us.

anlamlar.en: to keep something
ornekler: Hang on to your ticket – you'll need it later.
I'd hang on to those old photos.

anlamlar.en: to hold something tightly
ornekler: Hang on to the rail.
She hung on to my arm.

anlamlar.en: to start going somewhere
ornekler: We headed off early in the morning.
I'm going to head off now.

anlamlar.en: to prevent something from happening
ornekler: The government acted to head off a crisis.
We managed to head off the problem.

anlamlar.en: to leave a place to go somewhere
ornekler: We're heading out for dinner.
They headed out at dawn.

anlamlar.en: to listen to someone until they have finished saying what they want to say
ornekler: Please hear me out before you decide.
At least hear him out.

anlamlar.en: to suddenly have an idea
ornekler: She hit on the idea of selling cakes online.
We finally hit on a solution.

anlamlar.tr: (birine bir şey yüzünden) kin tutmak, bunu ona karşı kullanmak
anlamlar.en: to like someone less because of something they have done
ornekler: He made a mistake, but I won't hold it against him.
Don't hold it against me.

anlamlar.en: to manage to keep a job
ornekler: He can't hold down a job for more than a month.
She holds down two jobs.

anlamlar.en: to keep something at a low level, or to stop someone moving
ornekler: We must hold down prices.
It took three men to hold him down.

anlamlar.en: to put your hand or an object forward
ornekler: She held out her hand.
He held out a ticket to the guard.

anlamlar.en: to continue to defend yourself or to refuse to give in
ornekler: The town held out for three months.
The workers are holding out for more pay.

anlamlar.en: to have hope
ornekler: I don't hold out much hope of finding it.
Doctors are holding out hope for a recovery.

anlamlar.en: to hold something tightly, or to keep something
ornekler: Hold on to my hand.
The team held on to their lead.

anlamlar.en: to search everywhere for someone or something until you find them
ornekler: The police hunted down the escaped prisoner.
I hunted down an old copy of the book.

anlamlar.en: to accept an opportunity quickly and eagerly
ornekler: She jumped at the chance to study abroad.
I'd jump at an offer like that.

anlamlar.en: to continue working hard at something
ornekler: Keep at it and you'll succeed.
He kept at his studies despite the problems.

anlamlar.en: to not tell someone something
ornekler: I think she's keeping something back.
The police kept back some details.

anlamlar.en: to stay away from something
ornekler: Keep back from the edge of the platform.
The crowd was told to keep back.

anlamlar.en: to stop something from increasing
ornekler: We must keep costs down.
Try to keep your voice down.

anlamlar.en: to prevent someone from doing something
ornekler: The noise kept me from sleeping.
I could hardly keep from laughing.

anlamlar.en: to not tell someone something
ornekler: He kept the bad news from his parents.
Don't keep secrets from me.

anlamlar.en: to do what you have promised or planned
ornekler: We must keep to the plan.
Please keep to the speed limit.

anlamlar.en: to not move away from a subject or path
ornekler: Keep to the point, please.
Keep to the path in the forest.

anlamlar.en: to cause the death or end of many living things or ideas
ornekler: The cold winter killed off many plants.
The new law could kill off small businesses.

anlamlar.en: to refuse someone or an offer, or to drink something quickly
ornekler: She knocked back the job offer.
He knocked back his coffee and left.

anlamlar.en: to pretend that something is not serious by laughing about it
ornekler: He laughed off the criticism.
She tried to laugh off her mistake.

anlamlar.tr: (birine) sözle ya da fiziksel olarak saldırmak, giydirmek
anlamlar.en: to attack or criticize someone angrily
ornekler: The coach really laid into the players after the match.
She laid into him for being late.

anlamlar.en: to happen in the period before an event
ornekler: In the weeks leading up to the exam, I studied every day.
What led up to the argument?

anlamlar.en: to tell someone a secret
ornekler: Don't let on that I told you.
She knew the answer but didn't let on.

anlamlar.en: to become weaker or stop
ornekler: The rain didn't let up all day.
The pressure at work never lets up.

anlamlar.en: to be going to happen in the future
ornekler: Difficult times lie ahead.
Who knows what lies ahead?

anlamlar.en: to listen to a conversation without the speakers knowing
ornekler: Someone was listening in on our phone call.
I didn't mean to listen in.

anlamlar.en: to get money or food from someone or something in order to live
ornekler: He's 30 and still lives off his parents.
They live off the land.

anlamlar.en: to experience a difficult event or period and survive it
ornekler: My grandparents lived through the war.
We lived through some hard times.

anlamlar.en: to accept a difficult or unpleasant situation
ornekler: I don't like the noise, but I can live with it.
She has to live with the pain every day.

anlamlar.en: to put something in a safe place and lock it, or to put someone in prison
ornekler: She locked away her jewelry.
He should be locked away for life.

anlamlar.en: to think about something that happened in the past
ornekler: I look back on my school days with happiness.
Looking back on it, it was a great year.

anlamlar.en: to visit someone for a short time, especially to check that they are all right
ornekler: I'll look in on Grandma on my way home.
Can you look in on the baby?

anlamlar.en: to hope that someone will provide help or advice
ornekler: Students look to their teachers for guidance.
We look to you for support.
